headline: Spatial methylomes and isoform atlases resolve cell states within intact tissue
label: Spatial Single Cell Profiling
summary: Spatial readouts now extend beyond transcriptomes to DNA methylation and polyadenylation isoforms, resolving cell states in embryos and human tissue.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving cell identity and state in intact tissue by pairing spatial measurement with molecular or morphological readouts. SmC-seq extends spatial profiling to DNA methylation, generating genome-wide methylomes at near single-cell scale in mouse post-implantation embryos and decidua. A poly(A)-isoform-aware snRNA-seq and Xenium reference of adult human bladder adds an isoform layer, defining 22 cell types and 23,489 polyadenylation sites, with fibroblast niches placed spatially. On the analysis side, spatially smoothed quantification is benchmarked for per-cell marker aggregation in imaging mass cytometry, addressing spillover correction and cell typing. CELTIC, a context-dependent model, infers organelle localization from label-free microscopy and handles out-of-distribution cells in mitosis and colony contexts. The new element is the extension of spatial measurement into epigenomic and isoform-level layers.
